We are seeking an experienced Switches Project manager to join our engineering team at an OEM company. The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, development, and validation of interior switch components for automotive applications. This role involves working with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality, reliable, and innovative switch solutions that meet customer and regulatory requirements.

The ideal candidate will have prior experience in the automotive sector, specifically with OEM or Tier 1 suppliers, and be well-versed in key product development activities such as DVP (Design Validation Plan) and DFMEA (Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis).

Key Responsibilities

Support Technical expert in the design, development, and validation of interior switch systems, ensuring they meet functional, quality, and safety standards for automotive applications.

The switches include following but not limited to stalk control, start-stop switch, DNR switches etc.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams including design, electrical, software, and quality departments to develop innovative switch technologies.

Work & manage the design and development of switches into vehicle platforms, from concept to production, ensuring all technical requirements are met.

Prepare and execute DVP (Design Validation Plan) and support testing phases to ensure switches meet rigorous performance criteria.

Conduct DFMEA (Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) to identify and mitigate potential risks and failures in the design phase.

Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and ensure adherence to best practices and industry standards.

Collaborate with suppliers and vendors to ensure timely delivery of components and resolve any technical issues that may arise.

Contribute to product design reviews and ensure compliance with relevant automotive standards and regulations.

Track and report on project progress, ensuring timely delivery of design milestones and final product release.

Actively participate in the development of cost-reduction initiatives and improvements in the product lifecycle.

Required Skills

Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Automotive Engineering (or related field).

Minimum 5+ years of experience in automotive switch system design, with a focus on interior switch components.

Proven experience working with OEM or Tier 1 automotive suppliers.

Strong knowledge of automotive engineering processes, including DVP and DFMEA methodologies.

Hands-on experience with switch design, testing, and validation processes.

Familiarity with CAD tools (e.g., CATIA, Siemens NX, SolidWorks) and design verification tools.

Strong understanding of automotive electrical and mechanical systems.

Experience in working within cross-functional teams and managing technical projects from concept to production.

Excellent problem-solving skills with a strong ability to identify, analyze, and resolve design challenges.

Preferred Skills

Experience with automotive interior switch design for specific vehicle types (e.g., luxury, electric vehicles).

Familiarity with the latest automotive trends, including HMI (Human-Machine Interface) and touch-based switch technologies.

Advanced knowledge of material selection and process engineering for automotive components.

Knowledge of regulatory requirements such as ISO 26262 (functional safety), ECE regulations, and other automotive standards.

Experience with supplier management and working within a global supply chain.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

At Baxter, our mission to save and sustain lives is at the heart of everything we do. In this role, you will lead complex, cross-functional programs that support the delivery, reliability, and lifecycle performance of infusion pump systems used in patient care.

The Senior Program Manager is the core team leader and single point of program accountability for assigned Infusion Systems pump programs. This role translates product, customer, quality, regulatory, and business priorities into integrated execution plans and drives timely decisions across global teams.

You will partner with R&D Engineering, Systems Engineering, Software, Quality, Regulatory, Medical, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Service, Commercial, Finance, and external partners to deliver program commitments in a highly regulated medical device environment.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead complex infusion pump programs across the full product lifecycle, including new product development, software and firmware releases, sustaining engineering, compliance, cost improvement, and product obsolescence initiatives.
Own program scope, timelines, budgets, resources, quality, and risk management, ensuring successful delivery from initiation through implementation and closeout.
Direct cross-functional teams and drive alignment across engineering, manufacturing, regulatory, quality, commercial, service, and supply chain functions to achieve program objectives.
Develop and maintain integrated program plans, managing dependencies, critical paths, milestones, resource allocation, and launch readiness activities.
Establish program governance processes, lead reviews and decision forums, and provide timely escalation and resolution of complex program issues and risks.
Identify, assess, and mitigate technical, regulatory, quality, manufacturing, supplier, cybersecurity, and commercial risks while driving structured problem-solving and data-based decision making.
Communicate program status, milestones, budgets, risks, and recovery plans to senior leadership and stakeholders, influencing decisions and securing resources without direct authority.
Ensure compliance with design controls, quality systems, and regulatory requirements while supporting product roadmaps, continuous improvement initiatives, PMO best practices, and program management capability development.

Expertise in program planning and execution, including critical path management, financial management, risk mitigation, structured problem solving, and data-driven decision making.
Working knowledge of FDA Quality System Regulations, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62304, and applicable medical device quality and regulatory standards.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence across global matrix organizations; PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification preferred.

new_jobs.title: Business Analyst, Cisco Partner Incentive - Hybrid
new_jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 10/28/2026

The preferred location for this position is North Carolina, operating under a hybrid work model, though we are open to flexible, US-based hybrid arrangements for the right candidate.

Meet the Team

The Partner Incentive Team drives business capabilities, engagement and enablement for Cisco Partners across planning, rules definition, rebate calculation and reporting. Our team integrates expertise in CRM architecture, data governance, partner/distribution compensation, and AI-driven automation. We focus on delivering value for Cisco’s partners and distributors with speed and excellence. Using Agile and hybrid methodologies, we support transformational initiatives and optimize the business (OTB) to ensure our partners’ automation requirements are met with precision.

Your Impact

Responsibilities

You will act as a bridge between strategic business outcomes and complex data, drive operational excellence, and build strong relationships with business and IT partners to advance shared strategic goals. You will be responsible for:

Process & Data Analysis: Assist business functions by modeling internal processes, rules, and data flows to develop solid value cases for critical initiatives.
Data Intelligence: Generate complex reports and analyses from cross-functional sources to substantiate business decisions and provide actionable recommendations.
Trend Synthesis: Identify patterns within datasets, pinpoint key drivers (product, sentiment, segment, etc.), and communicate synthesized results to partners.
Requirements Definition: Partner with Business Stakeholders and SMEs to translate business problems into clear use cases and requirements.
Operational Optimization: Identify and implement opportunities for process improvement through rigorous analysis of business drivers and current practices.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Foster alignment between product teams and leadership, ensuring multi-functional needs are understood, communicated, and addressed.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Data Science/Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience), plus 5+ years of professional experience in Business/IT Consulting, Data Management, or Business/Functional Analytics.
Demonstrated experience analyzing, delivering, or optimizing workflows across at least two core business capability domains (e.g., Order Management, Incentive Compensation, Sales Performance Management, Distribution Compensation, or Business Reporting).
Hands-on experience applying business operations disciplines, including end-to-end process and data mapping, business problem decomposition, process improvement, change management, and risk identification.
Practical experience delivering projects within Agile frameworks (e.g., Scrum, Kanban, SAFe), including user story creation, backlog prioritization, or sprint execution.
Proven experience conducting quantitative data analysis, data interrogation/elicitation, and defining functional requirements in collaboration with cross-functional business and IT partners.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in enterprise business process design and governance, with fluency in multiple technology domains (network/infrastructure, data, applications/middleware).
Professional certification or hands-on experience with enterprise SPM or incentive compensation tools (e.g., Varicent, Xactly, Anaplan, CallidusCloud, or Salesforce).
In-depth expertise in data analysis, including usage of reporting tools (e.g., Business Objects) and advanced Excel features.
Proven track record of driving organizational change, managing multi-project portfolios, and successfully executing complex business transformations across diverse cross-functional teams.
Practical experience exploring and implementing AI tools, automated workflows, or intelligent productivity practices to streamline business operations.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

Please see the Cisco careers site to discover more benefits and perks. Employees may be eligible to receive grants of Cisco restricted stock units, which vest following continued employment with Cisco for defined periods of time.

U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies:

10 paid holidays per full calendar year, plus 1 floating holiday for non-exempt employees
1 paid day off for employee’s birthday, paid year-end holiday shutdown, and 4 paid days off for personal wellness determined by Cisco
Non-exempt employees** receive 16 days of paid vacation time per full calendar year, accrued at rate of 4.92 hours per pay period for full-time employees
Exempt employees participate in Cisco’s flexible vacation time off program, which has no defined limit on how much vacation time eligible employees may use (subject to availability and some business limitations)
80 hours of sick time off provided on hire date and each January 1st thereafter, and up to 80 hours of unused sick time carried forward from one calendar year to the next
Additional paid time away may be requested to deal with critical or emergency issues for family members
Optional 10 paid days per full calendar year to volunteer

For non-sales roles, employees are also eligible to earn annual bonuses subject to Cisco’s policies.

.75% of incentive target for each 1% of revenue attainment up to 50% of quota;
1.5% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 50% and 75%;
1% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 75% and 100%; and
Once performance exceeds 100% attainment, incentive rates are at or above 1% for each 1% of attainment with no cap on incentive compensation.

For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid.
